I've been farming these 6 mu for five years now, and with my university background I try to think it through rather than just copy the neighbors — though I still watch what they do. My wife and I handle most of the work; her brother helps off-farm income covers some input costs, so I don't have to cut corners on fertilizer.

For winter wheat, I'll plant an improved variety — Jimai 22 has done well here. I plan about 20 kg N per mu split between basal and topdressing at jointing, 8 kg P2O5, and 6 kg K2O. Last year my neighbors who pushed N to 28 didn't get much more grain, so I settled on 20 — a little above what the extension station recommended at the STB demo, because I still worry about a late cold snap hurting tillering. Three irrigations: winter water, jointing, and grain-filling. Two pesticide sprays for aphids and powdery mildew. Rotary tillage after maize stubble.

For summer maize, I'll go with Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid — dense planting, around 4,500 plants per mu. About 18 kg N per mu (one basal, one at big trumpet stage), 5 kg P2O5, 6 kg K2O. One irrigation if rain is short, usually at tasseling. One pesticide application for borer. No-till direct seeding right after wheat harvest so I don't lose days.

I expect about 500 kg/mu wheat and 550 kg/mu maize — that's what I've averaged.
